subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this broad multi-agent collaboration stack in core, and if so which narrow slice should be sponsored first instead of landing a full orchestration layer?
rationale: The request spans core agent routing, persistent memory/session state, new budget configuration, and security boundaries; repository policy and VISION.md require maintainer direction before adding those surfaces.

options.title: Keep RFC, split sponsored slices
options.body: Leave this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor one narrow product/security-reviewed core or plugin-API slice at a time.

options.title: Move experimentation outside core
options.body: Treat blackboard, learned profiles, and orchestration experiments as plugins or external prototypes until a concrete missing OpenClaw API is identified.

options.title: Close as out of current scope
options.body: Close the umbrella if maintainers decide the whole direction conflicts with the current VISION.md guardrail against heavy orchestration layers.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC, split sponsored slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor one narrow product/security-reviewed core or plugin-API slice at a time.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest current-history signal on the subagent/session implementation and related security-sensitive context surfaces.
